newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK retail price inflation data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK retail price inflation data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK inflation data showing RPI was 2.7 percent year-on-year in October while RPIX (underlying inflation) was 3.3 percent (vs expected 3.1 pct).
"That's very bad news. The gilt markets aren't going to like it and it's certainly going to strengthen Eddie George's hand in pressing the government for another rate increase."

"Certainly a bad number, but in line with our expectations -- we expected food and energy to boost the numbers this month. Food and energy costs were very weak last year, particularly petrol prices, and they've gone up this year in the same month. The underlying situation probably still isn't as bad as all that but it's clearly negative for the gilt market."

"We didn't think it would ever come in as high as this. The figures are really quite bad...showing that retailers are now quite confident about putting up prices. It puts the inflation target in extreme jeopardy and is very negative for the market, particularly the short end."

"The RPIX is disappointingly robust and implies that the budget will have to very prudent if rates are not to be hiked again in front of the election. Price hikes were sufficiently broad-based to suggest that the recovery in consumer demand has finally started to gain the momentum to allow retailers to widen their profit margins. This does not bode well for upcoming inflation data and will clearly be seen as putting extra pressure on the Chancellor to tighten again soon."

"The BOE will certainly claim this report to be consistent with their calls for higher borrowing costs now. Speculation will certainly be on a 6.25 percent base rate at the next monetary meeting in December."

"Truly awful. The market was bracing itself to take the RPIX figures above three pct. It's a bad shock to the markets all round and it's a very logical reaction to see both gilts and short sterling sell off very heavily."

"RPI ex-MIPS are right at the top end of expectations. The numbers are bad whichever way you look at them. They reflect price falls from a year ago dropping out of the yearly comparison plus fresh price increases in many areas. Interesting comment from the Chancellor following the data that policy is set to hit the 2.5 percent inflation target. This must suggest that the probability of a December 11 rate increase is now significantly higher."
